title: Nepal-India Treaty of Peace and Friendship
reason: The Treaty of Peace and Friendship was signed in Kathmandu on 31 July 1950 between India and Nepal's Rana Prime Minister Mohan Shumsher, establishing close bilateral ties including provisions on free movement and defense cooperation. The treaty remains in force and is well documented.

title: End of Rana Oligarchy and Return of Democracy
reason: The Delhi Agreement of 7 February 1951 ended 104 years of Rana rule. King Tribhuvan returned to Kathmandu on 15 February 1951, formed a coalition cabinet, and announced democratic reforms, consistent with the event description.

title: Nepal Opens to the Outside World
reason: After the end of Rana rule in 1951, Nepal ended its strict isolation policy. An independent Ministry of Foreign Affairs was established in 1951 and Nepal began admitting foreign nationals and establishing diplomatic relations. The UK and India already had embassies, and other Western powers followed.

title: First Ascent of Mount Everest
reason: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest at 11:30 a.m. on 29 May 1953, becoming the first confirmed humans to do so. This is one of the most thoroughly documented events in mountaineering history.

title: Nepal Joins the United Nations
reason: Nepal was admitted to the United Nations on 14 December 1955 as the 75th member, by UN General Assembly resolution 995 (X), along with fifteen other nations including Austria, Ireland, and Italy.

title: King Tribhuvan Dies, Mahendra Ascends Throne
reason: King Tribhuvan died in Zurich on 13 March 1955 (some sources cite 9 March), and his son Mahendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev ascended the throne on 14 March 1955. Mahendra was indeed educated abroad and was known for his conservative views on direct royal governance.

title: First Five-Year National Development Plan Launched
reason: Nepal launched its First Five-Year Development Plan covering 1956–1961, prioritizing transportation (receiving nearly 30% of the budget), agriculture, and education. International donors including India and the UN funded a significant share under the Colombo Plan.

title: First General Elections — Nepali Congress Wins
reason: Nepal held its first general elections in February 1959 under universal adult suffrage. The Nepali Congress won 74 of 109 seats and B.P. Koirala became Nepal's first democratically elected Prime Minister on 27 May 1959.

title: Royal Coup — King Mahendra Dismisses Parliament
reason: On 15 December 1960, King Mahendra executed a royal coup, dismissing parliament, arresting Prime Minister B.P. Koirala and cabinet members, and banning political parties. The coup ended Nepal's first parliamentary democracy after 18 months.

title: Panchayat System of Governance Introduced
reason: King Mahendra formally introduced the Panchayat system on 5 January 1961 as a partyless tiered governance structure. It banned political parties and concentrated power under the crown, operating until 1990. A new constitution codifying it followed in 1962.

title: Nepal-China Boundary Treaty Signed
reason: A final Nepal-China boundary treaty was signed in Beijing on 5 October 1961 by King Mahendra and Chinese Chairman Liu Shaoqi, formally delimiting the 1,389 km shared Himalayan border including the Everest area. China provided road construction and economic aid in parallel.

title: Muluki Ain Legal Code Revised — Caste Discrimination Abolished
reason: The New Muluki Ain of 1963 revised the ancient legal code to abolish untouchability and make caste-based legal discrimination illegal, recognizing all Nepalis as equal under the law. Implementation remained uneven in practice, as noted in the description.

title: Land Reform Act Implemented
reason: Nepal's Lands Act of 1964 established land ceilings, protected tenant farmers (limiting rent to 50% of main crop), and provided for redistribution of surplus land. The reform was the most comprehensive land reform in Nepal's history, though implementation was partial.

title: King Mahendra Dies, Birendra Ascends Throne
reason: King Mahendra died of a heart attack on 31 January 1972 during a hunting trip in Chitwan. His 26-year-old son Birendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev ascended the throne. Birendra had been educated at Eton and Harvard, and was initially seen as potentially more progressive.

title: King Birendra Proposes Nepal as Zone of Peace
reason: King Birendra formally proposed declaring Nepal a Zone of Peace during his coronation ceremony in 1975. The proposal ultimately received endorsements from over 130 nations but India and the Soviet Union declined, consistent with the description's note about India refusing to endorse.

title: Sagarmatha National Park Established
reason: Sagarmatha National Park was established on 19 July 1976 under the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Act. It was inscribed as a UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site in 1979, making it Nepal's first such designation.

title: Referendum Narrowly Retains Panchayat System
reason: Nepal held a referendum on 2 May 1980 in which 54.99% voted to retain the Panchayat system versus 45.2% for multiparty democracy. Opposition parties alleged fraud, and King Birendra subsequently announced reforms including direct elections to the National Panchayat.

title: Nepali Congress Launches Civil Disobedience Campaign
reason: In late May 1985, the Nepali Congress launched a satyagraha (civil disobedience) campaign demanding restoration of multiparty democracy. Police arrested hundreds of activists, and the campaign built organizational capacity for the larger 1990 movement.

title: Major Earthquake Kills Over 1,000 Along Nepal-India Border
reason: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Nepal-Bihar border region on 21 August 1988, with a combined death toll of approximately 1,003 in Nepal and Bihar. It was the largest earthquake in Nepal since 1934.

title: India Imposes Near-Total Economic Blockade on Nepal
reason: India closed 19 of 21 border crossings in March 1989 after the two countries failed to renew trade and transit treaties, creating a near-total economic blockade lasting 13 months until April 1990. The blockade caused severe shortages and accelerated the democratic movement.

title: People's Movement I (Jana Andolan) Erupts
reason: The Jana Andolan (People's Movement) officially began on 18 February 1990, launched jointly by the Nepali Congress and the United Left Front demanding an end to the Panchayat system. Strikes and protests paralyzed the country over the following 49 days.

title: King Birendra Restores Democracy and Lifts Party Ban
reason: On 8 April 1990, King Birendra lifted the ban on political parties and accepted constitutional monarchy after 49 days of mass protests that killed over 50 people. The Panchayat system that had dominated Nepal for 30 years formally ended.

title: New Democratic Constitution Adopted
reason: Nepal promulgated a new constitution on 9 November 1990 establishing a constitutional monarchy with a multiparty parliamentary system. It guaranteed fundamental rights, created a Westminster-style parliament, and vested executive authority in an elected prime minister.

title: First Multiparty Elections Since 1959
reason: Nepal held its first multiparty general elections since 1959 on 12 May 1991. The Nepali Congress won 110 of 205 seats, and Girija Prasad Koirala became Prime Minister. The elections were broadly recognized as free and fair.

title: CPN-UML Forms Nepal's First Communist Government
reason: After mid-term elections on 15 November 1994, the CPN-UML won 88 of 205 seats and Man Mohan Adhikari was sworn in as Prime Minister on 30 November 1994, forming Nepal's first communist-led minority government. It lasted nine months before falling.

title: Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) Formally Constituted
reason: The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) was formally constituted in March 1995 from a factional split in the CPN Unity Centre, led by Pushpa Kamal Dahal (Prachanda) and Baburam Bhattarai, with the explicit aim of launching armed revolution.

title: Maoist Insurgency Begins — People's War Launched
reason: The CPN-Maoist launched its armed insurgency on 13 February 1996 with simultaneous attacks on police posts in Rolpa, Rukum, and Sindhuli districts. The civil war ultimately lasted until 2006 and killed approximately 13,000–17,000 people.

title: Counterinsurgency Operation Kilo Sierra Two Launched
reason: The Nepal Police launched Operation Kilo Sierra Two (Kilo Serra II) in 1998 as a counterinsurgency sweep across Maoist-controlled regions in mid-western Nepal. Fourteen human rights organizations documented extrajudicial killings, torture, and forced disappearances.

title: General Elections Held Amid Ongoing Insurgency
reason: Nepal held general elections in May 1999 despite the ongoing Maoist insurgency. The Nepali Congress won a majority and Krishna Prasad Bhattarai became Prime Minister. The Maoists called for a boycott but did not violently disrupt the polls.

title: Royal Massacre — King Birendra and Family Killed
reason: On 1 June 2001, Crown Prince Dipendra shot and killed King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya, and seven other royals at Narayanhiti Palace. Dipendra was declared king while comatose and died three days later; his uncle Gyanendra then ascended the throne.

title: Peace Talks Collapse — Nepal Army Deployed Against Maoists
reason: A ceasefire declared on 25 July 2001 led to three rounds of peace talks, which broke down on 23 November 2001 when the Maoists unilaterally withdrew and attacked police and army posts in 42 districts. The Nepal Army was deployed against the insurgency for the first time.

title: King Gyanendra Seizes Power — Parliament Dissolved
reason: On 4 October 2002, King Gyanendra dismissed Prime Minister Deuba and assumed executive power, citing incompetence. He also indefinitely postponed scheduled elections. Political parties across the spectrum condemned the move as unconstitutional.

title: Second Ceasefire Collapses — Human Rights Crisis Deepens
reason: A second ceasefire was announced on 29 January 2003 and led to three rounds of peace talks, but the Maoists officially withdrew on 27 August 2003 citing government bad faith after the RNA killed 19 people in Doramba. Over 1,000 died in the following four months.

title: King Gyanendra Seizes Full Executive Power
reason: On 1 February 2005, King Gyanendra dismissed the government, assumed direct executive power, declared a state of emergency, cut communications, and arrested political leaders. India, the US, and the UN condemned the move and military aid was suspended.

title: 12-Point Agreement Between Parties and Maoists
reason: Nepal's seven mainstream political parties and the CPN-Maoist signed a 12-point agreement in New Delhi on 22 November 2005, establishing a common front against royal autocracy and committing both sides to a constituent assembly and competitive multiparty democracy.

title: People's Movement II Topples Royal Autocracy
reason: The second People's Movement in April 2006 brought hundreds of thousands into the streets, with over 500,000 protesters on 21 April alone. After 19 days and at least 18 deaths, King Gyanendra reinstated parliament on 24 April 2006, ending royal political authority.

title: Comprehensive Peace Agreement Signed — Civil War Ends
reason: The Comprehensive Peace Accord was signed on 21 November 2006 between the government and CPN-Maoist, formally ending the decade-long civil war. Maoist fighters were confined to cantonment camps under UN monitoring and a framework for constituent assembly elections was established.

title: Interim Constitution Declares Secular Federal Republic
reason: Nepal promulgated the Interim Constitution on 15 January 2007, eliminating Nepal's status as a Hindu kingdom, declaring it a secular state, and committing to federalism. It consisted of 25 parts, 167 articles and provided the framework for constituent assembly elections.

title: Madhesi Uprising Demands Plains Representation
reason: A major agitation erupted in Nepal's southern Terai in early 2007 as Madhesi groups protested the Interim Constitution's silence on federalism and representation. Protests resulted in over 30 deaths and forced an April 2007 constitutional amendment committing Nepal to a federal system.

title: Constituent Assembly Elections Held
reason: Constituent Assembly elections were held on 10 April 2008 and the CPN-Maoist won the largest share with 220 of 575 elected seats. The elections included proportional representation provisions significantly increasing seats for women, Dalits, and ethnic minorities.

title: 240-Year Shah Monarchy Abolished — Republic Declared
reason: The Constituent Assembly voted on 28 May 2008 to abolish the Shah monarchy by 560 to 4 votes, declaring Nepal a Federal Democratic Republic. King Gyanendra vacated the palace within weeks, ending the Shah dynasty that had ruled since 1768.

title: Prachanda Resigns Over Army Chief Dispute
reason: Prime Minister Prachanda resigned on 4 May 2009 after President Ram Baran Yadav overruled his dismissal of army chief Rookmangud Katawal, calling it unconstitutional. The dispute exposed fundamental tensions between civilian authority and the military.

title: Maoist Combatant Integration Partially Resolved
reason: A deal signed on 1 November 2011 provided three options to PLA combatants: integration, voluntary retirement, and rehabilitation. Approximately 1,400 fighters were symbolically integrated into Nepal's security forces, with the majority accepting retirement or rehabilitation packages.

title: Constituent Assembly Dissolved Without Constitution
reason: The Constituent Assembly was dissolved on 28 May 2012 by Supreme Court order after it failed to complete the constitution within its extended mandate. Four years of deliberation collapsed over unresolved disagreements on federalism and ethnic politics.

title: Second Constituent Assembly Elected
reason: Nepal held its second Constituent Assembly election on 19 November 2013 with high voter turnout. The Nepali Congress won the most seats with 105 of 240 first-past-the-post seats, while the Maoists fell from first to third place, reflecting voter frustration.

title: Gorkha Earthquake Kills ~9,000, Devastates Heritage Sites
reason: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck on 25 April 2015 killing 8,962 people (approximately 9,000 as stated), injuring over 21,000, and destroying nearly 900,000 buildings. Historic monuments in Kathmandu's UNESCO World Heritage Sites were severely damaged.

title: New Constitution Promulgated — Federal Democratic Republic
reason: Nepal's Constituent Assembly adopted a new constitution on 20 September 2015, declaring a federal democratic republic with seven provinces. It was immediately contested by Madhesi and Tharu groups who opposed the provincial demarcation and claimed under-representation.

title: India Blockade Follows Constitution Protests
reason: Following the September 2015 constitution, Madhesi protesters blockaded border crossings and India effectively closed most checkpoints, creating a severe fuel, medicine, and cooking gas shortage. The blockade lasted approximately five months and deepened anti-India sentiment.

title: Nepal Pivots to China After India Blockade
reason: In March 2016 Nepal signed a Transit Transport Agreement with China granting access to four Chinese seaports and land ports, providing an alternative to Indian transit routes. Nepal also formally joined China's Belt and Road Initiative, reflecting a strategic realignment following the blockade.

title: Federal and Local Elections Held Under New Constitution
reason: Nepal held local, provincial, and federal elections in 2017 — the first under the 2015 constitution and the first local elections in twenty years. The CPN-UML and Maoist Centre electoral alliance won decisive majorities, securing nearly two-thirds of federal seats.

title: Nepal Communist Party Formed by UML-Maoist Merger
reason: The CPN-UML and CPN-Maoist Centre formally merged on 17 May 2018 to create the Nepal Communist Party, with KP Sharma Oli and Prachanda as joint chairmen. The combined party held a near two-thirds parliamentary majority. It was later dissolved by the Supreme Court in March 2021.

title: Nepal Revises Maps to Include Kalapani Territory
reason: The territorial dispute intensified when India released a new map in November 2019 showing Kalapani, Limpiyadhura, and Lipulekh as Indian territory. Nepal published its formal revised map in May 2020 and parliament passed a near-unanimous constitutional amendment enshrining the claim in June 2020. The 2019 date refers to the trigger event; the formal map revision was completed in 2020.

title: Nepal Communist Party Fractures — Political Crisis
reason: In 2020, the Nepal Communist Party experienced a severe internal power struggle between Oli and Prachanda factions. PM Oli dissolved parliament on 20 December 2020 in an unconstitutional move overruled by the Supreme Court in February 2021, and the party formally split with Prachanda expelling Oli.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Devastates Nepal's Economy and Tourism
reason: COVID-19 reached Nepal in 2020, collapsing the tourism sector (which had aimed for 2 million visitors under Visit Nepal 2020) with losses exceeding $330 million. Hundreds of thousands of migrant workers returned home, and the World Bank projected 31.2% of Nepalis at risk of extreme poverty.

title: General Elections Produce Fractured Parliament
reason: Nepal held federal and provincial elections on 20 November 2022, producing a hung parliament with no single party or pre-election alliance winning a majority. Prachanda broke from the Nepali Congress alliance and formed a coalition with KP Sharma Oli, taking oath as Prime Minister on 26 December 2022.

title: Magnitude 5.9 Earthquake Strikes Far-Western Nepal
reason: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake did strike Doti and Bajhang districts on 9 November 2022, but it killed only approximately 6–7 people, not 'over 150' as the event claims. The death toll of 150+ belongs to the November 2023 Jajarkot earthquake. The casualty figure is off by more than an order of magnitude, making the title substantially misleading.

title: Jajarkot Earthquake Kills Over 150 in Western Nepal
reason: A magnitude 6.4 (local scale) earthquake struck Jajarkot and Rukum West districts on 3 November 2023 at 23:47 NPT, killing 153 people and injuring at least 375. It was the deadliest earthquake in Nepal since 2015, occurring in one of the country's least developed regions.

title: Nepal's Hydropower Exports to India Accelerate
reason: In 2024, India approved imports of nearly 1,000 MW of electricity from Nepal and Nepal became a net electricity exporter for the first time in fiscal year ending mid-July 2024. Nepal also signed a 10-year 10,000 MW power trade deal with India in January 2024.
